_readme: status 'accepted' = verified as intentional; it stays out of the way.
status 'pending'  = real debt, still open. Also quiet — the gate is on NEW findings.
A finding missing from this file fails the run, so growth is loud while the backlog is not.
Remove an entry once the finding stops occurring; the checker reports stale entries too.
The 2026-07-25 pass took this from 58 findings to 18. Everything structural is gone:
0 import cycles in src/shared, 0 layer violations, 0 dead IPC channels, 0 orphaned
modules that were not deliberate, and every storage key and duplicated export that
had two owners now has one. What remains is 14 accepted entries and 3 pending ones,
and all 3 are the same honest shape: a pure layer that is built and tested but has
no consumer yet, which its own phase report already records as its boundary.

duplicate-export:canUndo.note: Two unrelated undo stacks (renderer action history, CSV editor). Same verb, different domain — not shared logic.

duplicate-export:clearAll.note: Generic store verb on two unrelated stores (clipboard history, notifications).

duplicate-export:LANG_LABELS.note: TranslateContent's list is translation *target* languages; i18n/core's is UI languages. Deliberately independent — CLAUDE.md keeps those two selectors separate.

duplicate-export:pushHistory.note: Two unrelated history stacks, same verb — as canUndo.

duplicate-export:THEMES.note: readerSettings' THEMES is reader typography themes; theme.ts's is app colour themes. Different things, similarly named.

duplicate-export:qbitTransfers.note: main/scraper/qbittorrent.ts is the real WebUI call; scraper/data/fixtures.ts is the sample-data generator the mock port still uses for profiles with no client configured. Same noun, opposite sides of the port boundary — main may not import the renderer.

duplicate-export:translate.note: renderer/translator.ts translates study text; i18n/core.ts translates UI chrome. Unrelated by design.

duplicate-storage:jp-booted.note: One writer (App.tsx), one reader (BootScreen). Handoff, not co-ownership.

duplicate-storage:jp-os-personalization-.note: customCss.ts reads osPersonalization's blob only to honour the customCssEnabled gate at boot; documented inside bootCustomCss().

duplicate-storage:jp-user-css.note: This is the <style> element id, shared by the module that creates it and the one that removes it on reset. Not a storage key — it matches the jp- convention by coincidence.

orphan-module:src/renderer/motion/index..note: Barrel for the motion framework; consumers import the leaf modules directly. It costs nothing and is the documented public face of that folder.

orphan-module:src/main/anki/apkgReadWork.note: A process entry point, not a library — the same case as src/main/dictionary/importWorker.ts below, one classification weaker because no test imports it either. Its real caller is utilityProcess.fork() in apkgReadHost.ts, which names it by built path ('.vite/build/apkgReadWorker.js' via apkgReadWorkerPath), a runtime string the static import graph cannot follow. forge.config.ts builds it as a fourth Vite target, so a broken entry fails the build. Its logic is deliberately not here: everything testable lives in apkgCollection.ts, which src/main/__tests__/apkgReadOffMainLoop.test.ts imports directly, and that suite asserts the forge entry still exists — without it the worker is never built and every deck read silently falls back to parsing on the main event loop, which is the ANKI_DECK_WORKBENCH_PLAN.md gate 9 freeze this module exists to prevent.

orphan-module:src/main/flashcardTtsWorke.note: A process entry point, not a library — the same case as src/main/anki/apkgReadWorker.ts above. Its real caller is utilityProcess.fork() in flashcardTtsHost.ts:76, which names it by built path ('.vite/build/flashcardTtsWorker.js' via flashcardTtsWorkerPath at :24), a runtime string the static import graph cannot follow. forge.config.ts:216 builds it as its own Vite target, so a broken entry fails the build; the packaged artifact was measured at 5,970 bytes under out/jp-study-app-win32-x64/resources/app/.vite/build/. It exists so Japanese neural synthesis never runs on the main event loop — the 2026-08-29 USER FEATURE DIRECTIVE's offline-TTS outcome — and the testable half lives in src/main/flashcardAudio.ts, which the focused suites import directly.

orphan-module:src/main/anki/localDeckApk.note: A process entry point, not a library — the same case as src/main/anki/apkgReadWorker.ts above. Its real caller is utilityProcess.fork() in localDeckApkgHost.ts:11, which names it by built path ('.vite/build/localDeckApkgWorker.js' via localDeckApkgWorkerPath at :5), a runtime string the static import graph cannot follow. forge.config.ts:222 builds it as its own Vite target, so a broken entry fails the build; the packaged artifact was measured at 4,992 bytes. It authors the real APKG for a local deck's audio off the main loop; the testable half is src/main/anki/localDeckApkgCore.ts, which src/main/__tests__/localDeckApkgRoundTrip.test.ts imports directly.

test-only-module:src/main/llamaHostWorke.note: A process entry point, not a library — the same case as src/main/anki/apkgReadWorker.ts above. Its real caller is utilityProcess.fork() in llamaHost.ts, which names it by built path ('.vite/build/llamaHostWorker.js' via llamaHostWorkerPath), a runtime string the static import graph cannot follow. forge.config.ts builds it as a fifth Vite target, so a broken entry fails the build. Without that entry the fork exits 1 and every model load silently falls back to loading llama.cpp into the main process — which is the +534.6 MB / +3,349 handle residue this module exists to keep out of main. Re-keyed from 'orphan-module' to 'test-only-module' on 2026-08-25: src/main/__tests__/llamaAbortedGeneration.test.ts now imports it, so the checker sees an importer and reclassifies. That import is deliberate and is the point — boss audit 2026-08-25 Finding 2 was a guard in this file that no test could reach, and Finding 1 in the same audit was an unreachable guard nobody noticed was dead. The module is MORE covered than when it was an orphan, not less; the residency policy still lives in llamaContextPool.ts / llamaModelPool.ts / llamaBackend.ts, which their own suites import directly.

test-only-module:src/renderer/data/media.note: Named 'fixtures'. Test data is meant to be test-only.

test-only-module:src/shared/filesApp/rou.note: FILES_APP_PLAN.md gate 6's evidence: one row per Files-app capability naming where it is still reachable WITHOUT the Files app. The test IS the consumer, deliberately and by the same pattern as theme/tokens.ts above — a parity claim nothing re-derives is a comment, and shared/__tests__/filesAppRouteParity.test.ts re-derives every row from AppSection.tsx, both enumerator registries and the named module's own source. Marked 'pending' rather than 'accepted' because it should stop being test-only: the natural app consumer is the per-item 'also reachable in <section>' affordance that gate 10's planForPath open path and gate 12's reveal both want, and when that lands this entry comes out rather than being re-justified.

test-only-module:src/shared/i18n/catalog.note: CLAUDE.md says so explicitly: 'for tooling and tests only; importing it from app code puts every language back in the bundle'.

test-only-module:src/renderer/theme/toke.note: The typed mirror of tokens.css and the source THEME_TOKEN_REFERENCE.md is generated from; PHASE_1_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md and UI_UX_CORE_SHELL_EXECUTION_PLAN.md §12 both say to keep it in sync. It was an orphan — nothing read it, so nothing noticed drift. renderer/__tests__/themeTokenMirror.test.ts now checks every mirrored token against the CSS, which is why it reads as test-only: the test is the consumer, deliberately.

test-only-module:src/shared/episodeProce.note: §1 episode processing: built and tested, no consumer. The old reason — 'the settings UI edits the rules; nothing applies them, because no connector exists' — is STALE and was corrected 2026-08-19: a connector exists and all ten fields act on rows, via main/scraper/episodeProcessingRules.ts wired into both build paths (engine.ts:408, :493). Audit F5 is closed. This module stays test-only for a different and deliberate reason, stated in that file's header: it parses the DOM-extraction shape (ExtractedEpisode, with filler/recap/language and a numeric resolution), while the engine deals in EpisodeRow, which has none of those in that form. Round-tripping rows through the extraction shape to reuse it would drop real fields, so the behaviours are implemented against the shape the engine actually has. Closes when a DOM-extraction path calls it or it is deleted.

test-only-module:src/shared/mediaProvide.note: §7 sync journal, built and tested, no consumer. The original note blamed 'provider execution is out of scope', but provider execution now exists (Jikan/AniList metadata, Jimaku/OpenSubtitles subtitles). The real reason is different: this is a cross-device sync-envelope subsystem, and the app has no cross-device sync at all — no deviceId, no sync surface, no consumer for mediaProviderSyncPersistence or Resolution either. Wiring it would mean inventing that feature and adding a write path nothing reads. Left intact as designed, unfinished work.

test-only-module:src/shared/mediaWorkspa.note: ADR-003's exit gate. The allowlist must be empty and the adopted-surface list is what mediaWorkspaceI18n.test.ts parses — a gate whose only consumer is its own test is the point, not an accident.

test-only-module:src/main/dictionary/imp.note: A process entry point, not a library. Its real caller is utilityProcess.fork() in importIpc.ts, which names it by built path ('.vite/build/importWorker.js' via importJobs.dictionaryImportWorkerPath) — a runtime string the static import graph cannot follow, exactly like src/main.ts and src/preload.ts. forge.config.ts builds it as a third Vite target, so a broken entry fails the build rather than going unnoticed. The test import is of runDictionaryImport/attachDictionaryImportWorker, the two halves that are testable without a child process.

test-only-module:src/shared/subtitleFusi.note: The EN→JA fusion plan's F7 ship gate. Its real consumer is tools/fusion-eval.cjs, which esbuild-bundles this file at run time by path — the same kind of runtime reference the static import graph cannot follow as importWorker.ts, and the same pattern tools/grammar-audit.cjs and tools/i18n-check.cjs already use. It is deliberately not imported by the app: the harness scores the pipeline from outside it, needs real media and the Whisper runtime, and must not become something product code can call. If tools/fusion-eval.cjs is ever deleted, this becomes a genuine orphan and should be deleted with it.

test-only-module:src/renderer/components.note: Same L2 boundary the LiquidAppScaffold.tsx entry used to describe — that entry is now DELETED, because the Files app (renderer/components/filesapp/FilesApp.tsx) is a real product surface built on the spine, which is exactly the condition its note said would close it. The dock is the compact-width home for the rail's routes, which the scaffold drops below its `medium` breakpoint; it and AdaptiveRail/ContextToolbar (reachable through it) complete §5.2's primitive list. The Files app fills the rail from the scaffold directly and does not hand its routes to a dock, so this one is still unimported. Closes when a surface passes its compact breakpoint with routes to relocate.

Same L2 boundary as LiquidDock.tsx above. Fills the scaffold's inspector slot and carries the required close path (control, Escape, caller state) plus focus return. The Files app passes its own details pane into the scaffold's `inspector` slot rather than using this primitive, so nothing imports it yet. Closes when a surface needs the dismissable inspector rather than a permanent one.

test-only-module:src/shared/filesApp/not.note: FILES_APP_PLAN.md gate 7's evidence, at a finer grain than routeParity.ts: one row per Notebook STREAM naming the Files enumerator that indexes it and the section that still shows it. Test-only for the same reason and by the same pattern as routeParity.ts above -- shared/__tests__/filesAppNotebookAbsorption.test.ts re-derives the stream vocabulary from renderer/notebookTimeline.ts, the enumerator ids from both registries, the route from AppSection.tsx and every symbol from the named module. Marked 'pending', not 'accepted': its natural app consumer is the same per-item "also reachable in <section>" affordance routeParity is waiting on, plus a Files-app diagnostic for the two streams the index cannot see (plan, transcript). When either lands this entry comes out rather than being re-justified.
